titulek: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon
popis: Scientists have discovered that the stickiness of underwater “marine snow” plays a surprisingly important role in how much carbon reaches the deep ocean. Gooier particles resist bacterial breakdown and can transport more than six times as much carbon to the depths, revealing an unexpected connection between ocean slime and Earth's climate.

titulek: Regional climate change approaches Paris limits
popis: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02797-5 It has been surprisingly difficult to calculate how much warming different regions of the Earth have experienced since pre-industrial times. Now, research shows that in most land regions, the temperature thresholds that governments agreed to in Paris to keep below are already dangerously close.

titulek: All IPCC AR6 regions are close to their 1.5 °C- and 2 °C-equivalent warming limits
popis: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02790-y Climate targets are set for global temperatures, but what they mean regionally is less clear. Here the authors quantify the amount of human-induced warming in individual IPCC regions and find that, by 2025, they had reached 90–94% (65–76%) of their expected warming levels at the 1.5 °C (2 °C) global warming thresholds.
